subject: Private Offer — tiered annual prepay & ramp schedule questions
messages:
From: Maya Kline <maya.kline@microsoft.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, Jake Turner <jake.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Draft private offer for Acme — annual prepay options attached

Hi Tessa / Jake,

Following our call earlier, attaching the draft Azure Private Offer for Acme. The seller-side template includes two pricing structures: a) 1-year step-down prepay with monthly true-ups and b) a 3-year annual prepay with tiered discounts tied to committed spend bands.

Key points for your team to confirm:
- Can Acme commit to a 12- or 36-month term? We need the exact legal entity and billing contact for longer terms.
- For the 3-year option we proposed a 10% year-1 discount, 12% year-2, 15% year-3 on list rate (applies to Reserved SKU units).
- True-up cadence is annual, with an option for an interim Q2 true-up if year-to-date usage exceeds 110% of billed run rate.
- We added a performance safeguard: Azure will allow a one-time downgrade to a compatible model family if SKU availability is constrained — subject to notice.

Please review pages 3–5 for the pricing bands and page 7 for required Marketplace metadata. I've attached the offer PDF and a short calculator we use for ramp scenarios.

If Acme prefers a staircase ramp (phased commit increases), we can model credits that shift between years; that will change the effective blended discount.

Next steps: If you confirm term & preferred ramp, I can convert the draft to a Private Offer and send for signature.

Thanks,
Maya Kline
Azure Marketplace — Strategic Sales
Attachments: ACME_Azure_PrivateOffer_v1.pdf, redwood-prepay-calculator.xlsx
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Kline <maya.kline@microsoft.com>, Jake Turner <jake.turner@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft private offer for Acme — annual prepay options attached

Maya — thanks for the draft and calc. looping in Karthik and Marcus from our pricing & renewal team to weigh in on structure. Quick internal notes for Acme:

Jake / Elena — the buyer-side ask: Acme is aiming to hit a 3-year prepay but needs a firm ramp schedule that protects cash flow in year 1. Their FP&A asked for a front-loaded credit (higher vendor credit in year 1) with steady true-ups. They also want explicit language for a mid-term model fallback if there are supply issues.

From our side:
- We prefer the 3-year because it protects unit economics, but prefer the effective discount to be weighted toward year 1 (helps their cash visibility).
- Can Azure support a true-up window at 6 months (not just annual) for accounts showing >110% consumption vs committed run rate? That flexibility is important for variable retail seasonality.
- Need to confirm how Marketplace invoicing will reflect allocated credits vs consumed usage (important for our reconciliation).

Karthik / Marcus — can you review the attached calc and propose two concrete options we can present to Acme: Option A (cash-friendly for buyer: heavy year-1 credit, conservative year-3 uplift) and Option B (balanced: even discount progression but with a Q2 true-up trigger).

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Head of Marketplace Sales, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft private offer for Acme — annual prepay options attached

Thanks Tessa — reviewed the calc. I sketched two proposals (summary below) — attaching a redline of the PDF with band numbers (see attachment stub).

Option A — Buyer-cash-friendly (our recommended sell to win):
- 3-year term; committed spend bands: $500k / $1.25M / $2.5M over 3 years (annualized as 166k / 416k / 833k).
- Yearly effective discounts (off list): 18% / 12% / 8% for years 1/2/3 respectively (front-loaded savings).
- Year 1 advanced credit applied at invoice time; true-up windows at 6 and 12 months. Interim true-up only used to invoice additional consumption (no retroactive price changes).
- Early termination: pro-rated refund of unused credit after year 1 only if Acme reduces committed band by >50% (safeguard to avoid gaming).

Option B — Balanced (lower initial hit on Redwood economics):
- 3-year term; same bands.
- Yearly discounts: 12% / 13% / 15% (slightly backloaded).
- Annual true-up only, but offer an optional Q2 provisional true-up (non-billing) to forecast consumption with a reconciliation at 12 months.

Open question for Azure: can Marketplace metadata support a year-by-year credit line item (so Acme gets clear invoicing) or do credits need to be presented as a single upfront prepay allocation? That affects accounting for Acme.

Attached: internal_redline_ACME_offer.pdf (redline).

Karthik
Pricing Lead — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft private offer for Acme — annual prepay options attached

Tessa / Karthik / Maya — thanks for the fast turnaround. Couple of points from Acme finance & procurement:

1) Cash visibility: Acme can do a 3-year commitment but wants at most 25% of total payment due in year 1. Is there a way to restructure the prepay schedule so that their cash outlay is capped (e.g., split year 1 into two equal invoices or apply a deferred credit to year 2)?

2) True-up cadence: They prefer the 6-month provisional forecast + 12-month reconciliation approach (i.e., Option B with the provisional Q2 check) rather than hard billing at 6 months.

3) Legal asks that any fallback SKU substitution requires 30 days notice and a documented migration path with equivalent performance metrics.

If you can send a revised side-by-side that meets the cash cap (<=25% in Y1) and preserves the accounting clarity (credit line items), we can take to CFO next week.

Regards,
Jake Turner
Head of Cloud Procurement — Acme Retail Solutions
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@acme.com>, Maya Kline <maya.kline@microsoft.com>

Subject: Re: Draft private offer for Acme — annual prepay options attached

Jake — appreciate the clarity. Action plan from Redwood/Azure side:

1) Karthik & Marcus will produce a revised two-column comparison (Option A / Option B) that enforces a Year-1 cash cap of <=25% by modeling a split invoice and a deferred credit line in the Marketplace calc. Expect that doc by EOD 2027-05-27.
2) Maya — can Azure confirm the Marketplace presentation for credits (line-item vs allocated prepay)? If line-item credits are not supported, we will include a reconciliation exportable CSV for Acme to match invoices.
3) On fallback SKU substitution: agree to 30-day notice and require an agreed migration runbook with perf baselines; Marcus will draft minimal language for the Private Offer.
4) I'll prepare a short email for Acme CFO with the commercial summary and the DocuSign placeholder link once options are finalized.

Attachments: will circulate the updated comparison and the redlined offer (separate PDF).

Thanks all — Tessa
